questions.question: If x = 7/2 is a rational number and y = sqrt{27} , an irrational number, then x + y is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Irrational**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Property: The sum of a **rational number** and an **irrational number** is always an **irrational number**.

Given: x = 7/2 (Rational) and y = √27 (Irrational).

Logic: Rational + Irrational → **Irrational**.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = 7/2 = 3.5 (A **rational number** with a terminating decimal expansion)

y = √27 = √(9 × 3) = 3√3 (An **irrational number** with a non-terminating, non-recurring decimal expansion)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/652d0710c1bb112e3cacceee22ad0a9c54296de59715c39bc5eb025c06770d70.png] 

⇒ x = 3.5

⇒ y = 3 × 1.7320508...

⇒ y ≈ 5.1961524...

⇒ x + y = 3.5 + 5.1961524...

⇒ x + y = 8.6961524...

Since the sum results in a decimal expansion that is **non-terminating** and **non-recurring**, the resulting number is **irrational**.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Rational and Irrational

The product of a **non-zero rational number** and an **irrational number** is always **irrational**.

Sum of two Irrational Numbers

The sum of two irrational numbers is **not always irrational**; it can be rational (e.g., √2 + (−√2) = 0).

Rational Number Definition

A number that can be expressed in the form **p/q** where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

questions.question: If a number is rational, it cannot be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rational and Irrational numbers are **mutually exclusive** sets.

A number can either be expressed as a fraction p/q (Rational) or it cannot (Irrational).

Natural numbers, Whole numbers, and Integers are all **subsets** of Rational numbers.

Since a number cannot belong to both sets simultaneously, a rational number can never be irrational.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A number is rational.

**Definition:** A rational number is any number that can be written in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f73e7e8ead91b0dde2dd850338ab651e6b36476d8db7081773b142cf8223e1a.png] 

⇒ **Natural numbers** (1, 2, 3...) can be written as 1/1, 2/1, 3/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Whole numbers** (0, 1, 2...) can be written as 0/1, 1/1, 2/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Integers** (...−2, −1, 0, 1, 2...) can be written as −2/1, −1/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Irrational numbers** are those that cannot be expressed as p/q (e.g., √2, π).

⇒ If a number is in the Rational set, it is physically impossible for it to be in the Irrational set.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Real Number System

Real numbers are divided into two distinct groups: Rational and Irrational. Their intersection is an empty set.

Decimal Representation

Rational numbers have decimals that either **terminate** (e.g., 0.5) or **repeat** (e.g., 0.333...). Irrational numbers have **non-terminating** and **non-repeating** decimals.

Subsets of Rational Numbers

The hierarchy is: Natural Numbers ⊂ Whole Numbers ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rational Numbers.</p

questions.question:
What will be the number of zeros at the end of the square of the following numbers?
(i) 70
(ii) 500
Choose the correct option:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The number of zeros at the end of a square is always double the number of zeros in the original number.

(i) 70 ends in 1 zero → 70² ends in 1 × 2 = 2 zeros.

(ii) 500 ends in 2 zeros → 500² ends in 2 × 2 = 4 zeros.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 zeros in (i), 4 zeros in (ii).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (i) 70 and (ii) 500.

**Formula Used:** (a × 10ⁿ)² = a² × 10²ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2cbedf2a986fbaceed4c8466b465b8c23d578afed555b1bb5ca95701ceac84d.png] 

⇒ For (i) 70: 70² = 70 × 70 = 4900

⇒ Number of zeros at the end of 4900 = 2

⇒ For (ii) 500: 500² = 500 × 500 = 250000

⇒ Number of zeros at the end of 250000 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 2 zeros in (i), 4 zeros in (ii).**

**__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Trailing Zeros

A perfect square always ends with an even number of zeros. If a number ends in an odd number of zeros, it cannot be a perfect square.

Zeros in Cubes

If a number ends in n zeros, its cube will end in 3 × n zeros. For example, 10³ = 1000 (3 zeros).

Unit Digit Rule

The square of any number can only end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9. It can never end in 2, 3, 7, or 8.</p

questions.question: If ₹1,200 earns ₹216 as interest in 3 years, what is the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Rate (R)** = (**Simple Interest** × 100) ÷ (**Principal** × **Time**)

**Rate** = (216 × 100) ÷ (1200 × 3)

**Rate** = 216 ÷ 36 = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,200

**Interest (I)** = ₹216

**Time (T)** = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest** = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c47c0a2d8ea44d8fd683c2d8f9cf78113934b5987597862aec25dd8e4435721.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Simple Interest** for 3 years = ₹216

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1 year = 216 ÷ 3 = ₹72

⇒ **Rate of Interest (R)** = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100

⇒ **R** = (72 ÷ 1200) × 100

⇒ **R** = 72 ÷ 12 = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

The interest remains constant every year and is calculated as SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

Amount is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Simple Interest**: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Rate and Time Relation

For a fixed **Principal**, the **Interest** is directly proportional to both the **Rate** and the **Time**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about a rhombus?

options.text: All four sides are of equal length

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A rhombus is a special parallelogram where all four sides are of equal length.

Unlike a square, its interior angles do not need to be 90°.

Opposite sides are always parallel to each other.

Diagonals of a rhombus always bisect each other at right angles (90°).

**∴ The correct answer is All four sides are of equal length.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Quadrilateral is a Rhombus.

**Properties of a Rhombus:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f98d5affd80606a4b557fa1a7ea931ff8c2586fbf83b0917abe500f659ba5925.png] 

⇒ Property 1: All four sides are equal in length (AB = BC = CD = DA).

⇒ Property 2: Opposite sides are parallel (AB || CD and BC || AD).

⇒ Property 3: Opposite angles are equal (∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠D).

⇒ Property 4: Diagonals bisect each other at 90°.

**∴ The correct answer is All four sides are of equal length.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Rhombus

The area is calculated as 1/2 × d₁ × d₂, where d₁ and d₂ are the lengths of the diagonals.

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter is 4 × side, similar to a square.

Relation between Side and Diagonals

The relationship is given by the formula: 4 × side² = d₁² + d₂².</p

questions.question: What is area of a rhombus which has diagonals 10 cm and 8 cm?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

Area = (1/2) × 10 × 8

Area = 5 × 8 = 40 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first diagonal (d₁) = 10 cm

Length of second diagonal (d₂) = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rhombus = (Product of diagonals) / 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29c9f2afd18f4d6406144c4d02a912be1a77d17b10fdc321cdad0d0b661d4d0e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (d₁ × d₂) / 2

⇒ Area = (10 × 8) / 2

⇒ Area = 80 / 2

⇒ Area = 40 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rhombus

The perimeter is calculated as 4 × side. All four sides of a rhombus are equal in length.

Side and Diagonal Relationship

The side of a rhombus can be found using the formula: side = (1/2) × √(d₁² + d₂²).

Diagonal Properties

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).</p

questions.question: In a pair of concentric circles, a chord drawn in the larger circle just touches the smaller circle at a single point Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The chord is always longer than the radius of the smaller circle.
The chord is bisected at the point where it touches the smaller circle.
The chord lies entirely outside the smaller circle.
The chord passes through the center of both circles.

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A tangent to the inner circle is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

For the larger circle, this radius acts as a perpendicular from the center to the chord.

The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord.

**∴ The correct answer is The chord is bisected at the point where it touches the smaller circle.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two concentric circles with center O. AB is a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle at point P.

**Formula Used:** 1. Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. 2. Perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cd7608aa118887760a1036e1d48b7a7e4400fdc92b9ddb3c94c8ebe179e1aa0.png] 

⇒ Let the radius of the smaller circle be OP.

⇒ Since AB is a tangent to the smaller circle at P, OP ⊥ AB.

⇒ For the larger circle, AB is a chord and OP is the perpendicular from the center O to the chord AB.

⇒ According to the circle theorem, the perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord.

⇒ ∴ AP = PB.

**∴ The correct answer is The chord is bisected at the point where it touches the smaller circle.**

**__Additional Information__**

Chord Length in Concentric Circles

The length of the chord of the larger circle (radius R) that is tangent to the smaller circle (radius r) is given by 2 × √(R² − r²).

Tangent-Radius Theorem

A line is a tangent to a circle if and only if it is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency.

Perpendicular Bisector

The perpendicular bisector of any chord of a circle always passes through the center of that circle.</p

questions.question: A cylinder having radius of 5 cm and a height of 10 cm. Find its volume. (π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Volume** of **cylinder** = π × r² × h

Given: **radius** (r) = 5 cm, **height** (h) = 10 cm, **π** = 3.14

**Volume** = 3.14 × 5² × 10

**Volume** = 3.14 × 25 × 10 = 785 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 785 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** (r) = 5 cm

**Height** (h) = 10 cm

**π** = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

**Volume** of **Cylinder** = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d71b46bc02a9dd69f4454e778035dbe7d4217400aaae1ffcda2c6345ebf748f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Volume** = 3.14 × (5)² × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 3.14 × 25 × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 78.5 × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 785 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 785 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The area of the side surface of the **cylinder** is given by 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The sum of the **CSA** and the areas of the two circular bases: 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same **radius** and **height** as a **cylinder** has exactly one-third of its **volume**: (1/3)πr²h.</p

questions.question: If the height of a cylinder is doubled while keeping the radius the same, how does the volume change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doubles**__

 __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a cylinder (V) = πr²h.

When the radius (r) is kept constant, the volume is directly proportional to the height (h).

V ∝ h

If the height is doubled (h → 2h), the volume also doubles (V → 2V).

**∴ The correct answer is Doubles.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial radius = r | Initial height = h

New radius = r | New height = 2h

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17ea013c3b19ba4a4143accf3978eec1f5b35dad10aeea5b46ddcba86cf3bd2c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Volume (V₁) = π × r² × h

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = π × r² × (2h)

⇒ V₂ = 2 × (π × r² × h)

⇒ V₂ = 2 × V₁

**∴ The correct answer is Doubles.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effect of Radius Change

Since V ∝ r², if the radius is doubled while height is constant, the volume becomes 2² = 4 times the original.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

CSA of a cylinder = 2πrh. If the height is doubled, the curved surface area also doubles.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

TSA = 2πr(r + h). Doubling the height increases the TSA, but the exact change depends on the ratio of radius to height.</p

questions.question: A cylindrical concrete pillar has a radius of 0.5 m and a height of 4 m. If the curved surface is to be plastered at ₹180 per m², what will be the total plastering cost for 12 such pillars?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost = Number of pillars × (2 × π × r × h) × Rate

Total Cost = 12 × (2 × 3.14 × 0.5 × 4) × 180

Total Cost = 12 × 12.56 × 180

Total Cost = 150.72 × 180 = 27129.60

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27,129.60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius (r) = 0.5 m

Height (h) = 4 m

Number of pillars = 12

Rate of plastering = ₹180 per m²

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a2ed62208868906f8622c6a4ab5bda17c3baddaf3da59b91315581dd8af09aad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CSA of one pillar = 2 × 3.14 × 0.5 × 4

⇒ CSA of one pillar = 12.56 m²

⇒ Total CSA for 12 pillars = 12 × 12.56

⇒ Total CSA = 150.72 m²

⇒ Total Cost = Total CSA × Rate

⇒ Total Cost = 150.72 × 180

⇒ Total Cost = ₹27,129.60

**∴ The correct answer is ₹27,129.60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of Cylinder

The amount of space occupied by the cylinder: Volume = πr²h.

Area of Circular Base

The area of one flat end of the cylinder: Area = πr².

questions.question: How does the volume of a sphere change when its radius is doubled?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a sphere (V) is directly proportional to the cube of its radius (r).

Relation: V ∝ r³

When the radius is doubled, the new radius becomes 2 × r.

Change in volume = (2)³ = 8 times.

**∴ The correct answer is Eight times.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial radius of the sphere = r

New radius of the sphere = 2r

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/914543c11131583ce305f5577587062208725c9281a611012499ed63fb17d585.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Volume (V₁) = (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = (4/3) × π × (2r)³

⇒ V₂ = (4/3) × π × 8r³

⇒ V₂ = 8 × [(4/3) × π × r³]

⇒ V₂ = 8 × V₁

**∴ The correct answer is Eight times.**

**__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Sphere

The surface area (S) is given by 4 × π × r². If the radius is doubled, the surface area becomes 2² = 4 times.

Properties of a Hemisphere

Volume = (2/3) × π × r³ and Total Surface Area = 3 × π × r².

Ratio of Volumes

If the radii of two spheres are in the ratio a:b, then the ratio of their volumes is a³:b³.</p

questions.question: A hemisphere and a sphere have the same radius. The ratio of their total surface areas is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area of Hemisphere = 3πr²

Total Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr²

Required Ratio = 3πr² : 4πr²

Ratio = 3 : 4

**∴ The correct answer is 3:4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of hemisphere = Radius of sphere = r

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Sphere = 4πr²

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Hemisphere = Curved Surface Area + Area of circular base = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20f97393623240067209a56e82d22501ee7553327c6507c90fdbdf60314fcf09.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ TSA of Hemisphere = 3 × π × r²

⇒ TSA of Sphere = 4 × π × r²

⇒ Ratio = (TSA of Hemisphere) / (TSA of Sphere)

⇒ Ratio = (3 × π × r²) / (4 × π × r²)

⇒ Ratio = 3 / 4

**∴ The correct answer is 3:4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere and Hemisphere

Volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³ and volume of a hemisphere is (2/3)πr³.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The CSA of a hemisphere is 2πr², which is exactly half of the surface area of a sphere.

Ratio of Volumes

If the radii are the same, the ratio of the volume of a hemisphere to a sphere is 1:2.</p

questions.question: A triangle has sides of length 7 cm, 8 cm, and 9 cm. Find its perimeter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24 cm**__

 __Shortcut Trick__

The **Perimeter** of any **Triangle** is simply the **sum of the lengths of its three sides**.

Perimeter = 7 + 8 + 9 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side 1 (a) = 7 cm

Side 2 (b) = 8 cm

Side 3 (c) = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter (P) = a + b + c

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b483871c25501a165270d8f471c23a8a313878bde6db53a790eccadd810d5638.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter = 7 + 8 + 9

⇒ Perimeter = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Semi-perimeter

The semi-perimeter (s) is half of the total perimeter: s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Heron's Formula

The area of a triangle with sides a, b, and c is calculated as: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)].

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any valid triangle, the sum of any two sides must always be strictly greater than the third side.</p

questions.question: A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The length of the rectangle is twice its width. If the side of the square is 12 meters, what is the difference between the area of the square and the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter of square = 12 × 4 = 48 m.

Rectangle perimeter ratio (L : W = 2 : 1) → 2 × (2 + 1) = 6 units.

6 units = 48 m → 1 unit = 8 m.

Dimensions of rectangle = 16 m and 8 m.

Difference in area = 12² − (16 × 8) = 144 − 128 = 16 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 16 m².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of square (s) = 12 m

Length of rectangle (L) = 2 × Width (W)

Perimeter of square = Perimeter of rectangle

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of square = 4 × side

Perimeter of rectangle = 2 × (length + width)

Area of square = side²

Area of rectangle = length × width

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff2feb77783b30b1686ab161b4cc8debf3ced8dc266671c240c443b714396979.png] 

⇒ Perimeter of square = 4 × 12 = 48 m

⇒ Perimeter of rectangle = 2(L + W) = 48 m

⇒ 2(2W + W) = 48

⇒ 6W = 48 → W = 8 m

⇒ L = 2 × 8 = 16 m

⇒ Area of square = 12² = 144 m²

⇒ Area of rectangle = 16 × 8 = 128 m²

⇒ Difference in area = 144 − 128 = 16 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 16 m².**

**__Additional Information__**

Maximum Area Property

For a fixed perimeter, a square always has a larger area than any other rectangle.

Perimeter and Side Relationship

If a square and rectangle have the same perimeter, the side of the square is the arithmetic mean of the rectangle dimensions: s = (L + W) ÷ 2.

Area Formulas

Area of Square = side² and Area of Rectangle = length × width. Units are always in square measure (m², cm², etc.).</p

questions.question: The average weight of 39 boys travelling to Ladakh is 30. If an fat boy with weight 130 kg join them. What will be the average weight of the group travelling to Ladakh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**32.5**__

 __Shortcut Trick__

Initial average of **39 boys** = **30**

Extra weight brought by **130 kg** boy = 130 − 30 = **100 kg**

Increase in average = Extra weight ÷ Total boys = 100 ÷ **40** = **2.5**

New average = 30 + 2.5 = **32.5**

**∴ The correct answer is 32.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of boys = **39**, Initial average = **30**

Weight of new boy = **130 kg**

**Formula:**

**Average** = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5cbd437a116c342bd0d4b088283f1fcd9750d6b5f142d710015133e10cc7f1e8.png] 
⇒ Sum of weights of 39 boys = 39 × 30 = 1170 kg
⇒ Total weight including new boy = 1170 + 130 = 1300 kg
⇒ Total number of boys = 39 + 1 = 40
⇒ New average weight = 1300 ÷ 40 = **32.5**

**∴ The correct answer is 32.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the new average is Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Inclusion Rule

If a new member joins, New Average = Old Average + (Deviation ÷ New Strength).

Exclusion Rule

If a member leaves, New Average = Old Average − (Deviation ÷ New Strength).</p

questions.question: If a student scored 18.75 marks out of 25, what is the fraction in simplest form?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply both numerator and denominator by 4 to eliminate the decimal.

18.75 × 4 = 75

25 × 4 = 100

Fraction = 75/100 = 3/4

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Obtained value = 18.75, Total value = 25

Formula: Fraction = Obtained Value ÷ Total Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b23b8cfaa35f3628c670b9d2324a7c0f2a54e9aca8cecf516cecf070507da586.png] 

⇒ Required Fraction = 18.75 / 25

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by 100 to remove decimals: 1875 / 2500

⇒ Divide both by 25: 75 / 100

⇒ Divide both by 25 again: 3 / 4

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simplest Form of a Fraction

A fraction is in its simplest form when the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the numerator and denominator is 1.

Fraction to Percentage

To convert any fraction into a percentage, multiply it by 100. Example: 3/4 × 100 = 75%.

Decimal Removal Rule

To remove a decimal with two places, multiply both the numerator and denominator by 10² (i.e., 100).

questions.question: The average weight of 10 students was calculated as 50 kg. Later, it was discovered that one student's weight was wrongly read as 40 kg instead of 60 kg. What is the correct average weight?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net difference in weight = Correct weight − Wrong weight

Net difference = 60 − 40 = 20 kg

Increase in average = Net difference ÷ Total students = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 kg

Correct average = Old average + Increase = 50 + 2 = 52 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 52 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students (n) = 10

Initial average weight = 50 kg

Wrongly read weight = 40 kg

Correct weight = 60 kg

**Formula Used:**

Correct Average = [ (Initial Average × n) − Wrong Value + Correct Value ] ÷ n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38cde61fde707d8779518791627bb366a0a0323d6ae65f9975ebce54dd6f0415.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial total weight = 10 × 50 = 500 kg

⇒ Correct total weight = 500 − 40 + 60

⇒ Correct total weight = 520 kg

⇒ Correct average weight = 520 ÷ 10

⇒ Correct average weight = 52 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 52 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For a series in AP, the average is simply (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Inclusion and Exclusion

If a new person joins, the New Sum = (Old Average × Old n) + New Value. The new average is New Sum ÷ (Old n + 1).</p

questions.question: 40% of the employees in a factory are workers. All the remaining employees are executives. The annual income of each worker is 390rs. The annual income of each executive is Rs. 420. What is the average annual income of all the employees in the factory together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Workers = 40%, Executives = 60%

Use weighted average directly

Average income = (390 × 40 + 420 × 60) ÷ 100

⇒ (15600 + 25200) ÷ 100

⇒ 408

**∴ The correct answer is ₹408.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Workers = 40%

Executives = 60%

Income of each worker = ₹390

Income of each executive = ₹420

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (x₁w₁ + x₂w₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂)

 40% Workers ₹390 60% Executives ₹420 Average = ₹408 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Assume total employees = 100

⇒ Workers = 40, Executives = 60

⇒ Total income of workers = 40 × 390 = ₹15600

⇒ Total income of executives = 60 × 420 = ₹25200

⇒ Total income = 15600 + 25200 = ₹40800

⇒ Average income = 40800 ÷ 100

⇒ = ₹408

**∴ The correct answer is ₹408.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When groups have different sizes, average = Total Value ÷ Total Number.

Alligation Method

For two groups, average can also be found using alligation ratios.

Percentage to Quantity

Assuming total population as 100 often simplifies percentage-based average questions.

Combined Average

Combined Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total observations).

questions.question: If P is 20% more than Q, and R is 20% less than Q, then P is what percentage more than R?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the **Ratio Method**:

P : Q = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5

R : Q = 80 : 100 = 4 : 5

Combining them, P : R = 6 : 4 = 3 : 2

P is more than R by (3 − 2) = 1 unit over base 2.

Required % = (1 / 2) × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P = Q + 20% of Q

R = Q − 20% of Q

**Formula Used:**

Percentage More = [(Value₁ − Value₂) / Value₂] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33eaa1eec38d5092f337fee447211b423a93e7534fc92fd375ceb8e8cb06fdcb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the value of **Q** be 100.

⇒ P = 100 + 20% of 100 = 100 + 20 = 120.

⇒ R = 100 − 20% of 100 = 100 − 20 = 80.

⇒ Difference between P and R = 120 − 80 = 40.

⇒ Required Percentage = (Difference / R) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (40 / 80) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 1/2 × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change Formula

The percentage change is calculated as [(Final Value − Initial Value) / Initial Value] × 100. Always identify the correct **base value** (the value after 'than').

Base Comparison Rule

If A is x% more than B, then B is [x / (100 + x)] × 100% less than A. This is useful for quick **inverse percentage** calculations.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Common fractions help in speed: 1/2 = 50%, 1/3 = 33.33%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, and 1/8 = 12.5%.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper is offering a 20% discount on a Mixer that originally costs Rs 400. What is the sale price of the Mixer?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Discount of 20% means the Sale Price is 80% of the original price.

Sale Price = 80% of 400

Sale Price = 0.8 × 400

Sale Price = 320

**∴ The correct answer is 320.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original Price (Marked Price) = 400

Discount Percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Sale Price = Original Price − (Discount% × Original Price)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2cda5a39e731e2684ac265089893b0073d2ede397e681ef6cb3653af0960688.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = 20% of 400

⇒ Discount Amount = (20/100) × 400 = 80

⇒ Sale Price = 400 − 80

⇒ Sale Price = 320

**∴ The correct answer is 320.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price at which an article is listed or printed on the label is called the Marked Price or List Price.

Discount Formula

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Formula: Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts a% and b% are given successively, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at ₹1200 and offers a discount of 10%, but still makes a profit of 8%. What is the cost price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 10) : (100 + 8) = 90 : 108 = 5 : 6

Given **MP** = 6 units = ₹1200 → 1 unit = ₹200

**CP** = 5 units = 5 × 200 = ₹1000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1200, **Discount** = 10%, **Profit** = 8%

**Formula:** **Selling Price (SP)** = MP × (100 − D%)/100; **Cost Price (CP)** = SP × 100/(100 + P%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59b76565a7a0ada174a0c72a5c11de2fb0febef1cd50d685d1231f4e8d5abe9d.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price** = 1200 × (100 − 10) ÷ 100

⇒ **Selling Price** = 1200 × 90 ÷ 100 = ₹1080

⇒ **Cost Price** = 1080 × 100 ÷ (100 + 8)

⇒ **Cost Price** = 1080 × 100 ÷ 108 = ₹1000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Profit and Cost Price

**Profit** is calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**. Selling Price = CP + Profit.

CP and MP Relation

The ratio CP/MP = (100 − D%)/(100 + P%) is a direct result of equating the two expressions for **Selling Price**.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 15 days. B is 50% more efficient than A. How many days will B take to complete the same work?

The correct answer is __**10 days**__

 __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of **A : B** = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3

Given **A** takes 15 days, so 3 units = 15 days ⇒ 1 unit = 5 days

Time taken by **B** = 2 units = 2 × 5 = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 15 days

Efficiency of **B** = 50% more than **A**

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

questions.question: If the ratio is 42 : 5 = 7x : 10. Then find the x.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given ratio: 42 : 5 = 7x : 10

Compare denominators: 10 is 5 × 2.

Therefore, compare numerators: 7x must be 42 × 2.

7x = 84 ⇒ x = 84 ÷ 7 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio 1 = 42 : 5

Ratio 2 = 7x : 10

Ratios are equal: 42 : 5 = 7x : 10

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43d806598ec4c3c39d0a59a74d21c33ecb4c7a92182ffac5f71cfad3f4cc9ebe.png] 

**Formula Used:**

If a : b = c : d, then a/b = c/d

Product of extremes = Product of means (a × d = b × c)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 42 ÷ 5 = 7x ÷ 10

⇒ 42 × 10 = 5 × 7x

⇒ 420 = 35x

⇒ x = 420 ÷ 35

⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Proportion Rule

Four numbers a, b, c, d are in proportion if a : b = c : d, which implies a × d = b × c.

Fourth Proportional

If a : b = c : x, then x is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c, calculated as x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Simplifying Ratios

A ratio remains unchanged if both its terms are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero number.</p

questions.question: A train travels at 72 km/h. What is its speed in meters per second?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18.

Speed = 72 × (5/18) m/s

Speed = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the train = 72 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91657d7863d2918f30bd2555b9c5d44f141bd212a369fbaa6c70e1c3c24a234a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

1 km = 1000 m

1 hour = 3600 seconds

Speed (m/s) = Speed (km/h) × (1000 ÷ 3600) = Speed (km/h) × (5/18)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed in m/s = 72 × (5/18)

⇒ Speed = (72 ÷ 18) × 5

⇒ Speed = 4 × 5

⇒ Speed = 20 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the given speed by 18/5.

Basic Speed Formula

Speed = Distance ÷ Time. Ensure that all units are consistent (km and hours or m and seconds) before calculation.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For constant distances at speeds a and b, average speed = 2ab ÷ (a + b).</p

questions.question: A man walks from A to B at 5 km/h and returns from B to A at 4 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When an equal distance is covered at two different speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the Harmonic Mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × x × y) / (x + y)

Here, x = 5 km/h and y = 4 km/h.

Average Speed = (2 × 5 × 4) / (5 + 4) = 40 / 9 ≈ 4.44 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from A to B (v₁) = 5 km/h

Speed from B to A (v₂) = 4 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/63b236210c0e34ace998b5b7b30079153b8e23a0af206b05f52d977f31e69dee.png] 

⇒ Let the distance between A and B be 'd' km.

⇒ Time taken to go from A to B (t₁) = Distance ÷ Speed = d / 5 hours.

⇒ Time taken to return from B to A (t₂) = Distance ÷ Speed = d / 4 hours.

⇒ Total Distance for the whole journey = d + d = 2d km.

⇒ Total Time taken = t₁ + t₂ = d/5 + d/4 = (4d + 5d) / 20 = 9d / 20 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 2d ÷ (9d/20)

⇒ Average Speed = (2d × 20) / 9d = 40 / 9 km/h

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 4.44 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 4.4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a person travels at speed v₁ for time t and speed v₂ for the same time t, the average speed is the Arithmetic Mean: (v₁ + v₂) / 2.

General Average Speed Formula

For any journey with different distances d₁, d₂ and speeds v₁, v₂, Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) / (d₁/v₁ + d₂/v₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = v₁ + v₂. In the same direction, relative speed = |v₁ − v₂|.
